page: The Vultr vhf-2c-2gb is an entry-level virtual instance within the High Frequency Compute family, configured with 2 shared x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel core via hyperthreading at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, supporting standard instruction sets such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory is provisioned at 2.0 GB of RAM, equating to 1.0 GB per vCPU, paired with a bundled 80 GB local NVMe SSD and a single complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations highlight a divergence between single-threaded compute tasks and systemic multi-threaded throughput. In single-core execution, the instance achieves 1425.29 on stress-ng and a gzip compression rate of 24.24 GB/sec, placing it within the median bracket of tested hardware. Conversely, multi-core and memory-heavy metrics fall into lower percentiles, with stress-ng multi-core recording 2786.09 and PassMark CPU reaching 3137.23. Memory bandwidth reflects entry-tier shared infrastructure limitations, measuring 18.67 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 12.65 GB/sec for writes. Application-level metrics reflect these hardware bounds, showing 2.3 million Redis SET operations per second, a static web serving throughput of 2.3 GB/sec, and low small-model LLM generation rates.

Given its minimal memory footprint and shared vCPU model, the primary hardware tradeoff lies in predictable multithreaded capacity and memory capacity versus accessible local NVMe storage. The vhf-2c-2gb serves cost-sensitive, low-footprint workloads including lightweight background utilities, personal web servers, modest microservices, staging environments, and basic CI/CD test runners that fit comfortably within 2 GB of memory.

Hardware capabilities include AVX and AES vector support alongside a 16 MB L3 cache. Benchmarking indicates moderate single-core efficiency, logging 1425.29 on stress-ng and 24.24 GB/sec in gzip compression, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth fall into lower percentiles due to its shared-core execution profile and 1:1 memory-to-core ratio. The bundled high-speed NVMe storage balances the constrained memory envelope, positioning this server for lightweight web hosting, low-traffic APIs, small microservices, and development environments.
